articles.title: Pro-Palestine philanthropist faces US extradition hearing in Spain
articles.summary: James ‘Fergie’ Chambers denies wrongdoing, while his wife urges PM Sanchez to grant him political asylum.
articles.body:
Madrid, Spain – The wife of a pro-Palestine philanthropist who faces extradition to the United States has urged the Spanish prime minister to grant him asylum, to save him from being sent to his own country.

James “Fergie” Chambers, a US citizen with a reported $250m net worth, has been charged with money laundering.

The US government’s case centres on Chambers’s alleged laundering of $7.5m, which he is said to have wired several years ago from a US bank account to Tunisia, where he lived at the time, allegedly using the cash to support Hamas. He is not charged with any “terrorism” offences and denies any wrongdoing.

“I am pleading with [Spanish Prime Minister Pedro] Sanchez to use his powers to ensure Fergie’s political asylum claim is expedited for urgent consideration by the panel of ministers,” his wife Stella Schnabel told Al Jazeera. “If [Sanchez] chooses not to act, he risks enabling [US President Donald] Trump to establish a precedent in Spain and across Europe which criminalises solidarity with the Palestinian people.”

Schnabel says that the money was to support Club Africain, a Tunisian football club, to pay off its debts and overdue salaries, to reconstruct a training centre and build pitches for youth sides.

Spain’s National Court will hear evidence from the US authorities on Friday, and a final decision will be made later.

Chambers, a self-proclaimed anti-imperialist, is also facing charges of riot and conspiracy to riot relating to a protest at an Israeli arms company in 2023 in the US, for which he could face up to 30 years of imprisonment.

Chambers was arrested in July in Ibiza as he and his partner, Schnabel, an actress, searched for a school for their son, after Interpol issued a Red Notice for his detention. Since his arrest, he has claimed asylum, alleging he is the victim of political persecution.

Chambers cannot be extradited until the asylum claim is resolved, and if it is successful, he cannot be extradited.

Lawyers for Chambers said mistranslations between the US criminal charge in English and the version presented to Spanish authorities in Spanish make the allegations seem more serious.

Under Spanish law, all extradition requests must be translated into Spanish.

The alleged mistranslations, which relate to protests in 2003 in the United States that targeted the US-based facilities of Elbit Systems, Israel’s largest weapons manufacturer, changed “direct action” to “direct violence”.

Lawyers also said there is no reference to violence in the original US criminal complaint, but the translated version submitted to Spanish authorities mentions “three fires” even though no fires are mentioned in the original text.

US authorities also changed the description of protesters’ “activation” of smoke canisters to “detonation”, which, defence lawyers say, is usually used to describe an explosive device, not the release of smoke canisters.

The most serious mistranslation, say defence lawyers, involved a conversation between third parties that in the original criminal complaint described Chambers as being part of a “global terrorism game”.

However, in the translated version submitted to Spanish authorities, this phrase is changed to “global terrorism activities”. Chambers has not been charged with any “terrorism” offences.

“It’s important to highlight that the US administration has not charged Fergie with material support for or financing terrorism or any terror-related offences, nor presented a shred of evidence that even a single cent has been used for violent or terrorist acts,” Aitor Martinez, one of the defence lawyers, told Al Jazeera.

“The reason not to charge him with those offences is clear: there is no evidence.”

If the court backs the US extradition request, defence lawyers for Chambers will appeal, dragging the case on longer.

However, the Spanish government’s Council of Ministers may have the last word on the case and could refuse to send him to the US if they believe the case is politically motivated.

The situation is complicated by the fact that Spain is holding an early election on November 29, which, according to the polls, the conservative People’s Party is likely to win, potentially requiring the support of the far-right Vox party.

Both right-wing parties may be more inclined to support extraditing Chambers than Spain’s Socialist prime minister Sanchez, an outspoken critic of Trump’s support for Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.

Chambers, 46, is heir to the Cox family, owners of the Atlanta-based Cox Communications. As part of a deal in which his family cut ties with him at the time, he sold stock back to his family worth about $250m in 2003.

Since then, he has funded about 100 projects in 20 countries, Schnabel said.

The US Department of Justice declined to comment when contacted by Al Jazeera.

Two of the three charges in the US complaint – riot and conspiracy to riot – are related to allegations that he funded the legal fees of activists arrested in the 2003 protests against Elbit.

Chambers has commented publicly on Israel and Gaza.

In the wake of the 2023 Hamas attacks on Israel, he posted on X about Israel’s response: “Stop calling it ‘collective punishment’/There’s nothing to be punished for/No faction of the Palestinian resistance, Hamas or other, has done *anything* wrong/It’s simply genocide/Like it has been.”

On the day of the court hearing, demonstrations will be held in support of Chambers outside Spanish embassies in London, Brussels. Amsterdam and Tunisia, where Chambers lived for some time.

articles.title: Oklahoma man, 73, executed for plotting murder of lover's husband, offers no last words
articles.summary: James Pavatt was pronounced dead after lethal injection for plotting the 2001 murder of Rob Andrew, who was gunned down in his garage just before Thanksgiving.
articles.body: An Oklahoma man convicted of plotting with his lover to kill her estranged husband 25 years ago was executed Thursday without uttering any final words. James Pavatt, 73, was put to death by lethal injection at the Oklahoma State Penitentiary in McAlester for the 2001 murder of Rob Andrew, a 39-year-old advertising executive who was gunned down in his garage while picking up his two young children just before Thanksgiving. Pavatt was pronounced dead at 10:12 a.m. local time, according to the Oklahoma Department of Corrections. Prison officials described the execution as "uneventful," adding that Pavatt had no last words, according to local news station KOKH. FLORIDA DEATH ROW INMATE USES LAST WORDS TO MAINTAIN INNOCENCE BEFORE EXECUTION For his last meal, Pavatt requested a strawberry milkshake and a barbecue dinner of smoked chicken, brisket, pulled pork, fried okra, baked beans and pickles, KOCO reported. Pavatt was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder. He had been having an affair with Rob Andrew's wife, Brenda Andrew, who was convicted in a separate trial and also sentenced to death. Weeks before the killing, Rob Andrew told police someone was trying to kill him after the brake lines on his car were cut. Brenda Andrew later claimed masked intruders shot her in the arm and fatally shot her husband at the Oklahoma City home the couple previously shared. Prosecutors, however, said she and Pavatt plotted the murder. The pair fled to Mexico with Brenda Andrew's two children after the shooting but were arrested three months later while re-entering the United States. At a clemency hearing last month, Pavatt maintained his innocence and claimed Brenda Andrew had manipulated him. ALABAMA GOVERNOR COMMUTES DEATH SENTENCE AS DOUBTS EMERGE ABOUT EVIDENCE IN MURDER CONVICTION "It was not until my trial that I began to see the extent to which I had been manipulated by Brenda," he told the board. "I can see why the jury believed that we were both involved in Rob's murder." Prosecutors maintained that both were equally responsible for the killing, regardless of who fired the fatal shots. In Texas, John Allen Rubio, 46, was set to be executed that evening for the 2003 stabbing and beheading of three young children he was raising in Brownsville. The victims were 3 years old, 14 months old and 2 months old. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Former pastor quits church ministry after decades, moves to Florida in 2020 to become Disney World bus driver, leaves after 2022 divorce and returns in 2026 after finding love again
articles.summary: After spending decades in church ministry, Michael Bowen decided to make a dramatic career change at 44, leaving his religious profession behind to pursue
articles.body: After spending decades in church ministry, Michael Bowen decided to make a dramatic career change at 44, leaving his religious profession behind to pursue his dream of working at Walt Disney World. He moved from New Jersey to Florida on January 1, 2020, and began working as a Disney bus driver in February. However, a divorce in 2022 forced him to leave Florida and relocate to Oregon. His love for Disney remained intact, and a new relationship eventually brought him back to Central Florida. In April 2026, at 50, Bowen returned to Walt Disney World, proving that it is never too late to start over.Bowen spent much of his adult life working in church ministry, a career he had pursued in his twenties largely to fulfil the expectations of a church mentor. However, by his forties, he was struggling with burnout and financial difficulties, even driving a school bus part-time to make ends meet.The idea of working at Disney World took shape during a Thanksgiving vacation in 2017. While sitting poolside at Disney's All-Star Resort in Florida, Bowen found himself dreading the winter weather back home in New Jersey. He also began thinking about the resort's bus drivers, whose work had fascinated him during previous visits."I was fascinated by the equipment that I saw on their dash and the little GPS and noticing the turn and seeing how they interacted with guests," Bowen told PEOPLE.Determined to change his life, he moved to Central Florida on January 1, 2020. However, the hiring process took several months, and obtaining a Florida driver's licence was among the requirements. After six weeks of anticipation, he finally joined Disney World as a bus driver in mid-February 2020."I loved every minute of it. It was like a dream come true... I would say, 'Just pinch me, because I can't believe this is real'," he recalled.2022 divorce forced him to leave his dream jobFor Bowen, working at Disney was a life-changing experience. The job provided him with stability, health insurance, paid leave, retirement benefits and a sense of fulfilment he had not experienced before.However, his personal life took an unexpected turn in 2022 when his marriage ended in divorce. The development prompted him to leave Florida and move to Oregon, forcing him to walk away from the Disney job he had spent years trying to secure."It was difficult because I love Disney. I spent years trying to get there, and I realized I had to leave knowing that I may never come back," he said.Despite the distance, Bowen continued nurturing his connection with Disney through his YouTube channel, Incognito Mouse, where he produced content centred on the resort and its attractions.New romance brings him back to Florida in 2026His passion for Disney also helped him find a new relationship. Through his content, Bowen met Barbie, 43, who shared his enthusiasm for the vacation destination. The two eventually fell in love, and in 2025, they decided to relocate, bringing Bowen back to Central Florida.While waiting for another opportunity at Disney, he worked as a bus driver for a company contracted to operate buses for Universal Orlando Resort.His efforts finally paid off in April 2026, when Bowen returned to Walt Disney World as a bus driver at the age of 50."I drive for the Most Magical Place on Earth. Every night, when I'm driving through Disney property, I get to see the fireworks as I'm driving down the road. I see Space Mountain or I see the Tower of Terror... You just can't get that anywhere else," he said.A little boy's gesture makes his job specialWhile driving a bus may not be the most glamorous position at the resort, Bowen believes the small interactions with guests make his work worthwhile. He recalled a little boy who once boarded his bus and presented him with two toy buses, an interaction that stayed with him."I don't get to play Jack Sparrow walking through the park. I don't get to be up on stage dancing or doing things. I drive a bus. It's not the most glamorous job, but for this little boy, it meant everything," he said.His message for those looking to start overReflecting on his unconventional journey, Bowen believes people should not let age, financial difficulties, relationship troubles or professional setbacks stop them from pursuing their dreams.Taking inspiration from Walt Disney's famous words, "If you can dream it, you can do it," he said that making a fresh start often requires sacrifices and the support of people who encourage you."If you want it bad enough, you'll make it happen. You'll make sacrifices and you'll find other people around you who will motivate you," he added.For Bowen, leaving church ministry, rebuilding his life after divorce and returning to Disney World were all part of a journey that eventually led him to a career and lifestyle he had once only imagined.You use AI every day. articles.title: Is Outlook down? Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.summary: A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant’s suite of apps.
articles.body: CHICAGO — A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant’s suite of apps. As of around 1:30 p.m. ET, more than 120,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook — with many saying they couldn’t send and receive emails, or encountering delays. Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services. Microsoft said that it was investigating. In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.” Microsoft later added that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company said it would begin ”redistributing” traffic to help balance the load. Microsoft did not immediately provide further information. Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

articles.title: A Swiss heart surgeon who lost her Guinness collection title in 2024 has reclaimed it with 3,200 heart-shaped objects; Diana Reser has spent 25 years collecting everything from art to household items
articles.summary: For most people, a heart-shaped object might be a decoration, a piece of jewellery or a symbol of affection.
articles.body: For most people, a heart-shaped object might be a decoration, a piece of jewellery or a symbol of affection. For Swiss heart surgeon Diana Reser, however, it has become a lifelong passion that has filled her home and workplace with thousands of objects. From everyday household products to unusual artwork and souvenirs, her collection reflects both her medical profession and her fascination with the heart as a symbol of love and life.Reser has reclaimed the Guinness World Records title for the largest collection of heart-shaped items, with 3,200 objects officially counted on April 13, 2026, in Zollikon, Switzerland. According to a November 10 report published by Guinness World Records, she first secured the title in 2010 with 775 items but lost it in 2024 to American collector Susan West, whose collection contained 1,560 pieces. After continuing to collect for several more years, Reser has now more than doubled her previous record.Collection began when she was a medical studentReser's interest in heart-shaped objects began approximately 25 years ago, when she was studying medicine. After completing an internship in heart surgery, she decided to pursue the speciality as her profession. As news of her career ambitions spread, family members, friends and colleagues began giving her heart-shaped presents. The gifts gradually developed into a much larger collection, with new additions arriving even after she became a practising surgeon.Speaking to Guinness World Records, Reser explained how the gifts became a regular part of her life. "From that moment on when word spread about my dream job I received heart-shaped presents which goes on until today," she said. She eventually organised and categorised all 3,200 objects for the latest record attempt. Around half of the collection consists of gifts, while she has purchased many of the remaining pieces during her travels around the world.From household products to unusual keepsakesThe collection includes an extraordinary variety of objects, ranging from practical household items to decorative pieces and personal accessories. There are heart-shaped solar lights, car air fresheners, hair accessories, perfumes, soaps, jewellery and clothing. Her collection also includes artwork, ornaments and objects displayed throughout her home and office. She even has six heart tattoos.Describing the range of items to Guinness World Records, Reser said: "You name it, I have it. Basically everything you can use in your everyday life." Among the more unusual pieces are a heart-shaped Rubik's cube, a fully functioning stethoscope and a piece of the Berlin Wall. Two paintings are particularly special to her: a colourful Picasso-style artwork depicting three women holding a heart and a painting of a barn owl with a heart-shaped face, created by her sister.Despite having thousands of similar objects, Reser welcomes new additions. She told Guinness World Records that she cannot control what people choose to give her as presents and appreciates every new piece, even when she already owns something similar.Surgeon connects collection with heart health awarenessFor Reser, the fascination goes beyond collecting decorative objects. Her medical career and the symbolism associated with the heart are closely connected to her interest. She described the heart as a universal symbol of love, life and the soul. She also gave her growing fascination a name, calling it "heart-itis". She explained that once people begin consciously noticing heart shapes around them, they continue spotting them everywhere.Reser was also the first female heart surgeon to receive a professor title from a Swiss university, according to Guinness World Records. She has dedicated her collection to her family, friends, colleagues and patients who have contributed to it over the years. She also uses the recognition to encourage greater awareness of cardiovascular health. She recommended heart check-ups by the age of 50, or earlier for people with a family history of heart conditions. She also encouraged patients who need planned heart surgery not to be afraid of the procedure.A broken heart-shaped shower remains on her wish listEven with 3,200 objects, Reser still has items she hopes to find. One is the Heart of Eternity, a rare 27.64-carat blue heart-shaped diamond. However, her more immediate search involves a much simpler household object. She once owned a heart-shaped shower head, but it broke after falling, and she has been unable to find another one. She appealed to anyone who might come across one to let her know.Looking back at her record-breaking journey, Reser told Guinness World Records that she never really felt she had lost the title in 2024 because she believed her collection was already larger. She simply had not completed another official count. Her first record lasted 14 years. Now, she is curious to see how long her latest achievement will stand, joking that if it lasts longer, she will probably be retired by then.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why did Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resign, and who is Colette Kress?
articles.summary: Huang has stepped down amid allegations of extramarital affairs and Chinese espionage.
articles.body:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following allegations that he had extramarital affairs.

Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, has taken over as interim CEO while the company looks for a permanent replacement.

The company controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips and is one of the world’s most valuable companies.

Huang stepped down on Thursday following several days of intense scrutiny over his personal relationships and potential national security issues.

On Sunday, Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and to Nvidia employees.

Huang moved to the United States from Taiwan as a child. His wife, Lori, has been with him since before he co-founded Nvidia in 1993.

Nvidia’s board initially backed Huang, saying on Sunday that it had confidence in his leadership. It also launched an independent investigation into reports that he had been targeted by Chinese intelligence.

But on Wednesday, the Reuters news agency reported that the board was meeting to consider whether to remove him after further allegations of a relationship with Kimberly Powell, a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

The company announced his resignation on Thursday. Huang also resigned from the board, ending his 33-year tenure as chief executive.

Nvidia did not give a reason for his departure.

“Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound,” the board said in a statement, thanking him for his “immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry”.

What are the allegations involving Jensen Huang?

The allegations were related to reported extramarital affairs.

The first involved Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed, who is alleged to have worked for Chinese intelligence.

The allegations have raised questions about national security, particularly given Huang’s support for allowing Nvidia to sell advanced AI chips to China.

Separately, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him.

The second reported relationship raised concerns about a potential conflict of interest involving a senior executive.

Why are there national security concerns?

The controversy comes amid a debate in Washington over exporting advanced US AI chips to China.

Huang, 63, spent years campaigning against the restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China.

In December 2025, US President Donald Trump approved the export of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China, despite concerns that the technology could bolster Beijing’s AI capabilities.

The chips are about six times more powerful than the H20 models previously available to Chinese buyers.

Exports are subject to US inspections, limits on shipments, restrictions on military use and a 25 percent tariff.

According to Al Jazeera’s Osama Bin Javaid, Chinese companies reportedly ordered more than two million H200 chips, potentially worth $54bn.

“Worth remembering it’s orders, not completed sales,” he said.

Critics are concerned the technology could help China close the AI gap with the US.

The allegations raised questions about whether his personal relationships could have exposed sensitive information.

“There is no established evidence he knowingly assisted Beijing or that company secrets were compromised,” Bin Javaid noted.

Nvidia’s board has also said it has no reason to believe national security was compromised.

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia’s new interim CEO?

Kress has served as Nvidia’s chief financial officer since September 2013 and oversaw the chipmaker’s finances during a period of growth.

During her time at Nvidia, the company’s annual revenue rose from $4.13bn in fiscal 2014 to $215.9bn in fiscal 2026.

Before joining Nvidia, Kress held senior finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco.

She holds a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

Kress is also among the wealthiest self-made women in the US, according to Forbes.

In a statement following her appointment, Kress said she was committed to building on the foundation Huang had created over the past 33 years.

Will Colette Kress become Nvidia’s permanent CEO?

Nvidia’s board has appointed Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement and considers both internal and external candidates.

Trump has suggested former Apple chief executive Tim Cook as Huang’s successor.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump praised Huang’s work at Nvidia and said Cook was the person to replace him.

“A Legend replaces a Legend,” Trump wrote.

Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief executive in September and now serves as the company’s executive chairman.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, technology and cybersecurity analyst Ritesh Kotak said choosing Nvidia’s next CEO would be a decision for the company’s board.

“At the end of the day, it comes down to the board,” he said.

Kotak pointed to the differences between Apple, which primarily sells consumer technology, and Nvidia, whose chips power much of the AI industry.

There has been no indication that Cook is interested in the position.

Trump has defended Huang amid the allegations.

Reporting from the White House, Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher said Trump had offered a “very forceful defence” of the Nvidia cofounder, who accompanied him on a trip to China earlier this year.

Trump said he recently learned of the suspected spying scandal, although reports suggest he had been informed of the allegations before the trip.

Fisher said the president was likely to face further questions about “what he knew and when he knew it”.

Meanwhile, Huang’s departure has raised concerns about Nvidia’s future.

“He’s the captain that was steering the ship back since the early ’90s,” Kotak told Al Jazeera.

“These are big shoes that need to be filled,” he added.

Kotak said the resignation could create uncertainty among Nvidia’s employees and customers.

“If you’re Nvidia, if you’re the employees, if you’re a customer, I think you’re worried right now,” he said.

Clement Delangue, chief executive of Hugging Face, which Nvidia has agreed to acquire, reaffirmed his commitment to open-source AI following Huang’s resignation.

Meanwhile, Lloyd Blankfein, former chief executive of Goldman Sachs, reflected on Huang’s departure in a post on X.

“Sad about Jensen. Shakespearean,” he wrote, quoting former French President Charles de Gaulle: “The graveyards are filled with indispensable men.”

Huang’s departure has also raised questions about the wider AI industry. Nvidia is not only a major chip supplier but also an investor in companies that build and rent out AI computing infrastructure.

The company is also preparing to invest approximately $10bn in AI developer Anthropic as part of its planned stock market listing, expected next week.

Nvidia is in a difficult moment as it looks for a permanent CEO and faces increasing political scrutiny in Washington.

The hunt is now on for a permanent successor, and the board is open to both insider and outsider candidates, Nvidia said.

According to Reuters, several names are being discussed by industry watchers, including:

Kress, Nvidia CFO, analysts and investors have cited her experience, authority and deep relationships with Wall Street as assets that could help steer the company through the transition.

Nvidia executive Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing. He joined in 2004 and helped develop technology that transformed the company from a video game chipmaker into a leading force in AI hardware.

Rene Haas, Arm CEO , spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager.

Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s first-ever board chair, was appointed to the position following Huang’s resignation. Jones has served on Nvidia’s board since 1993, before the chipmaker went public. He also sits on the company’s audit and nominating and corporate governance committees.

Lisa Su leads AMD, one of Nvidia’s main competitors. If appointed, the announcement could represent a major disruption for AMD.

Sanjay Mehrotra, Micron CEO, has more than four decades of experience in the semiconductor industry and has worked closely with Nvidia, which uses Micron products.

And Cook, who took over at Apple shortly before cofounder Steve Jobs died in 2011, appeared as a potential candidate following Trump’s comments.

The leadership shake-up has also had an effect on the markets. Nvidia shares were down more than 14 percent at one point on Thursday before recovering some of that ground.

The major US stock indexes also closed lower.

“Investors seem to be moving past the scandal and putting their money elsewhere, shifting to other tech stocks,” Al Jazeera’s Kristen Saloomey reported from New York.

Meanwhile, US lawmakers are looking into the potential national security implications of Huang’s reported relationships.

articles.title: Democrats gather in Denver to debate party’s future after US midterm wins
articles.summary: Majority Democrats’ What’s Next conference brings lawmakers and potential 2028 contenders to Denver.
articles.body:
After winning control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, Democrats will descend on Denver on Thursday for a conference on the future of the party.

The two-day conference, titled What’s Next, presents itself as a forum to debate the direction of the party and will bring together potential presidential candidates for 2028, newly elected lawmakers, party strategists, and established Democratic leaders.

The gathering was planned in advance of the midterms by a new group called Majority Democrats, chaired by Massachusetts Representative Jake Auchincloss.

On its website, the moderate group presents itself as an alternative to “an old establishment” that “sells mediocrity disguised as moderation” and an activist left that “demands purity disguised as justice”.

The group says its members are “willing to challenge the establishment and break with their party when it means standing up for the people they actually represent.”

But some progressives question the organisers’ vision for the party, arguing it is not ambitious enough, including its backing of a public health insurance, which it calls “Medicare for Americans”, option over a Medicare for All system.

The conference comes as Democrats prepare to take control of both the House and the Senate in January, facing decisions about how to use their majorities to challenge Trump in the final two years of his presidency, and begin to look ahead to 2028.

Among the attendees who have been announced are Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and New Jersey Senator Cory Booker, all seen as potential contenders for the Democratic presidential nomination in the next election.

They will be joined by newcomers who flipped seats in the midterms last week, including Texas Senator-elect James Talarico and Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek.

Also attending are California Representative Ro Khanna, who has described himself as a “long-shot presidential candidate”, and Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, who has said he is “kicking the tires” on a possible 2028 run.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to be the next House speaker, is also on the list of confirmed attendees, despite scepticism among some on the party’s left about the party’s current leadership. He will speak on Friday about the 120th Congress, which begins next year.

Khanna and Van Hollen will join New Jersey Senator Andy Kim for a discussion on “The Trust Deficit,” while Shapiro and Senators Elissa Slotkin and Ruben Gallego are scheduled to speak about the next era of the Democratic Party.

Missing from the published speakers are high-profile progressive figures like Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Bernie Sanders.

Jeffries spoke on a range of topics including the House Democrats’ upcoming majority and the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. [File: Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images/AFP]

articles.title: Witkoff, Kushner to meet with Zelensky as Ukraine reports Starshield restrictions for second time
articles.summary: U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky this week amid reports the eastern European country’s access to Starshield satellite communications has been restricted for a second time. “I think progress was made. I think it was made earlier today,” Witkoff told CNN after meeting with…
articles.body:
U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky this week amid reports the eastern European country’s access to Starshield satellite communications has been restricted for a second time.

“I think progress was made. I think it was made earlier today,” Witkoff told CNN after meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Wednesday. “People didn’t think that we were going to restart trilateral. We’ve restarted it. We’ve set a new meeting.”

“This is what President Trump wants to see,” he said, adding that European allies would join the upcoming talks.

The envoy continued, “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved.”

Kushner, the president’s son-in-law, described their talks with Putin and other Russian officials as “very fulsome and detailed discussions on all the topics,” which he thinks “will inform hopefully the next multilateral discussions,” according to CNN.

The envoys’ meeting in Moscow occurred the same day Zelensky claimed in a post to social platform X that new restrictions were limiting the ability of Ukrainian interceptors powered by Starshield — the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink — to stop Russian projectiles traveling faster than 100 mph.

As a result, Zelensky said, the interceptors could not reach sufficient speed to down ​Russian jet-powered drones.

“This means more Russian strikes get through, and more of our people are killed by Russia. We are trying to get the details from the American side, but so far, we know very little,” Zelensky wrote.

The slowdown comes after similar Ukrainian Starshield outages in October sparked a firestorm in Washington, causing lawmakers to accuse the Trump administration of cozying up to Russia. At the time, Trump’s decision to waive a bipartisan Russian sanctions package named after the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) added to the furor.

Administration officials were quick to blame tech billionaire Elon Musk, of Tesla and SpaceX, for the slowdown — for which he later accepted blame despite initially denying the allegations. The CEO has not yet commented publicly on the latest outage.

Witkoff and Kushner are now headed to Dublin to meet with Zelensky after their visits to Moscow and Abu Dhabi — during which their trilateral talks with Ukrainian and Russian officials yielded a “large-scale” exchange of prisoners of war but did not culminate in a ceasefire or peace deal.

articles.title: A cheese that’s been sitting on a shelf for two years is named the world’s best
articles.summary: A 24-month-aged French Comté from JuraFlore has been named the world’s best cheese at the World Cheese Awards in Spain, beating 5,329 rivals
articles.body: What were you doing two years ago? Perhaps you voted in a pivotal election, or sang your heart out to the newly released movie “Wicked” at the cinema. Maybe you placed a wheel of cheese onto a cellar shelf in the Jura Mountains of eastern France … and waited. If it was the latter, then congratulations! That cheese could now be the best in the world, according to the judges of the prestigious World Cheese Awards, who gathered in Spain on Thursday to sample more than 5,000 varieties of dairy produce to crown a winner. Despite a tight final round against heavyweight contenders from Italy, Switzerland and Spain, the ultimate champion was a 24-month-aged Comté — a nutty, crumbly and deeply complex creation from France’s eastern border. “It is the complexity, obviously,” said Spanish expert Rafael Domínguez González — one of 14 super judges who each championed one cheese into the tense final round of the competition — of his chosen offering. “We see how it evolves in the mouth. It starts to develop in different layers of flavor, beautiful nutty layers. It definitely left a mark here.” The winning Comté, a hard cheese made from unpasteurized cow’s milk in the Franche-Comté region bordering Switzerland, was aged at Fort des Rousses by JuraFlore, a traditional family-run affineur (cheese maturer) founded in 1907. “It’s such a pleasure,” Franck Arnaud, a descendant of JuraFlore’s original founder, told the award ceremony via videolink. “We have 120 years next year and a family business all this time. It’s an amazing pleasure for me, this news, and I can’t wait to tell the others.” ‘I love this cheese’ After crossing the Pyrenees to arrive in the Spanish city of Córdoba, where this year’s awards were held, the winning wheel faced a much tougher journey through multiple judging rounds before reaching the final 14. A grand total of 5,330 cheeses from 45 countries made it to the competition hall, where they were laid out on a series of tables and assessed by an army of judges for taste, smell, appearance, texture and mouthfeel. “Super gold” prize winners from each table advanced to a second round of sampling before a live onstage tasting session picked the champion. It was close, though. With the 14 final judges each giving marks out of seven, the winning Comté finished neck-and-neck on 81 points alongside a Swiss mountain cheese — described as a “big, big boy” by cheese writer and event host Patrick McGuigan — and a younger French ewe’s-milk cheese. The Comté triumphed on a tie-breaker because it had the smallest range of scores. McGuigan said the winning cheese was greatly aided by its maturity, particularly when it came to its appetizing appearance. “You can see the color, that dark, dark golden color. That’s coming from time, basically,” he said in his onstage assessment. “Some people argue that time is the fifth ingredient in cheese. You’ve got your milk, your starter cultures, your rennet, your salt. But time can play a huge part in developing flavor. To me, that talks of summer pastures, that really golden color, cows eating grass…” While raw-milk cheeses face strict import rules in countries such as the United States over health concerns, aged varieties like Comté easily clear the FDA’s 60-day maturation requirement. Still, given that each wheel takes two years to produce, American cheese aficionados will have to move quickly to secure a slice of the winning batch before supplies run out. Those who manage should be in for a treat, according to judge Domínguez González. “I love my friends … I love my girlfriend, and I knew I love this cheese,” he said. “I’m very happy.”

articles.title: US releases report on $12bn from Venezuelan oil, mineral resources
articles.summary: The report seeks to address concerns about the Trump administration’s handling of revenue held in trust for Venezuela.
articles.body:
The United States Department of State has released a report detailing what it says the US has done with more than $12bn in revenue from Venezuelan oil and mineral resources, nearly a year after it abducted the country’s leader, Nicolas Maduro.

The disclosure is part of an effort to “promote transparency and accountability in the management of these funds”, says the 53-page report, released on Thursday.

In January, US forces conducted a raid on the Venezuelan capital of Caracas, capturing Maduro and his wife and bringing them to New York City, where they are currently facing charges related to drug trafficking and torture.

Venezuela’s then-vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, took over after Maduro’s abduction and has since made agreements with Washington that saw the US take a direct stake in profits earned from the export of oil and other mineral resources from the South American country.

Since removing Maduro from power, the Trump administration has sought to directly control who buys natural resources from Venezuela and who earns profits from those sales.

US President Donald Trump issued an executive order in January establishing special bank accounts that would hold revenue from those transactions, to be eventually distributed back to Venezuela in a controlled manner.

Trump has made Venezuela a central part of his political narrative, touting the revenue he said the US would receive from sales of the country’s oil during election campaigning in the run-up to the midterm elections that were held earlier this month. Venezuelan rights activists have expressed concern that Washington may give outsized importance to oil revenues and take little interest in backing democratic reforms after the removal of Maduro.

The report released on Thursday covers flows into and out of US-controlled accounts between January 3, 2026 and September 30, 2026. The State Department has also contracted private Washington, DC-based auditing firm KPMG to examine the transactions.

The US took in more than $12.26bn from “verified and approved entities engaging in authorized activities” in Venezuela during that time, according to the report. Most of that flow came from crude oil and petroleum-based revenue, but it also included deposits stemming from transactions involving gold, minerals, and fertilisers.

More than $12bn of that revenue has been disbursed as of September 30, with some $169m remaining in the account, according to the report.

The US initially set up an account in the Qatar National Bank in January to take in funds from entities looking to buy authorised oil and other minerals from Venezuela. Approximately $500m was initially deposited into that account, with almost all of it distributed back to Venezuelan entities by late January, when a separate, dedicated US Treasury-controlled account was set up to handle future transactions.

The current account, controlled directly by the US Department of the Treasury, has taken in more than $12bn in funds, from about 20 depositors, whose identities are redacted in the State Department’s report. Approximately 99 percent of those funds were related to the purchase of oil, according to the report.

By the end of September, the State Department report says, nearly all of those funds had been distributed to a set of Venezuelan banks, to be used in foreign exchange interventions, transactions where banks sell those dollars to reduce the amount of local currency floating around and prop up the currency’s value, in this case the Venezuelan bolivar.

The report is heavily redacted and does not provide details about the final recipients of the more than $12bn in funds that was distributed in Venezuela, although it does note that approximately $9.4bn went to “legal entities” and $2.9bn to “individuals”.

articles.title: Microsoft outage hits tens of thousands of users
articles.summary: Microsoft says servers unexpectedly went offline, disrupting Outlook email, Teams, Copilot and other services.
articles.body:
Thousands of Microsoft users reported trouble accessing their email and connecting to work apps after a widespread outage hit Outlook and other services on Thursday.

Reports of problems with Outlook, the company’s email client, climbed to about 130,000 on the outage tracking site Downdetector shortly after 1pm Eastern Time (18:00 GMT), with some users saying emails weren’t being sent or received, while others couldn’t open their inboxes.

By just before 3pm (20:00 GMT), that figure had fallen to about 77,000.

Users also reported having trouble accessing Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams and its AI assistant Copilot, along with other Microsoft 365 services. The company said the issues could impact users in any region.

Microsoft said on X that servers were unavailable and failing automatic health checks, putting pressure on those still operating. It said it was testing a configuration change to redistribute traffic that was elevated on parts of its infrastructure and restarting affected services to bring them back online.

“We’re working to safely return them to service,” the company said.

Microsoft did not state when it expected services to be fully restored.

articles.title: Minnesota yarn shop apologizes for selling 'Harry Potter' kits, donates proceeds to trans care group
articles.summary: A Minnesota yarn shop pulled all "Harry Potter" merchandise and donated its profits to a transgender care organization after backlash over J.K. Rowling's views.
articles.body: Needle & Skein, a yarn shop in Minnesota, apologized last week for selling "Harry Potter"-themed kits, calling the decision a "mistake." "We recently sold Harry Potter-themed kits, and we owe you a sincere apology," the business wrote on Facebook Saturday. "I’m a mom, and I read these books aloud to my child. Those evenings are some of my sweetest memories, and I think that warmth kept me from stopping to consider what carrying this merchandise would mean for our trans friends, neighbors, and customers. I made a mistake, and I’m so sorry," the statement continued. "Harry Potter" author J.K. Rowling has faced criticism in recent years over her opposition to policies allowing transgender women into certain female-only spaces. In an essay last month, Rowling doubled down on her stance, calling transgender activism "elitist to its core." NEW 'HARRY POTTER' SHOW POSTER GOES VIRAL AS FANS REACT TO UPCOMING SERIES BASED ON JK ROWLING'S BOOKS The store announced that it had removed the "Harry Potter" items from the shelves and donated all the proceeds to Point of Pride, an organization that provides support to transgender people. "We never meant to hurt anyone. But we can see that we did, and we are truly sorry to everyone who felt less welcome in a space that should always feel like home to you. You deserve better from us," the company said. Needle & Skein also shared an image showing its donation to Point of Pride, saying it donated three times the profits from its "Harry Potter" merchandise. The business also shared a link for followers to donate. Needle & Skein told Fox News Digital that the response to its apology had been largely positive, despite some doxxing and negative reviews. "Overall, the response has been positive, with people feeling that we were open, honest and appreciative," owner Gilah Mashaal said. JK ROWLING SAYS 'HARRY POTTER' STARS WHO CRITICIZED HER TRANS VIEWS CAN 'SAVE THEIR APOLOGIES' Fox News Digital reached out to Rowling for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Rowling has also faced boycott efforts from LGBTQ activists targeting her books and merchandise. Last year, a San Francisco bookstore announced that it would no longer be selling Rowling's books due to her views on gender. Christian Toto, host of the "Hollywood in Toto" podcast, told Fox News Digital that he doubted the owners of the Minnesota yarn shop understood exactly why Rowling's views were controversial. JK ROWLING CONFRONTS THE BBC FOR PUSHING 'PROPAGANDA' OVER ITS TRANSGENDER SPORTS HEADLINE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The media blurs many facts in our culture, like how 'immigration' isn't separated into two distinct camps — legal and illegal. Something similar likely is happening here. And for a yarn hobbyist to take such a stand is, well, the height of silliness on too many levels to count. Sadly, she's far from alone," Toto said.

articles.title: An Indiana man joined a two-hour pedal-pub tour, drank beer and fell while climbing off the 48-inch-high seat; five years later, an appeals court says the waiver he signed prevents his negligence claim
articles.summary: A leisurely afternoon exploring downtown Indianapolis on a pedal-powered pub tour ended with an unexpected injury and a lengthy legal battle for one
articles.body: A leisurely afternoon exploring downtown Indianapolis on a pedal-powered pub tour ended with an unexpected injury and a lengthy legal battle for one participant. What began as a two-hour outing with friends, complete with stops at local bars and restaurants, eventually turned into a lawsuit after a man fell while getting off the elevated bicycle-style vehicle. Five years later, the Indiana Court of Appeals has upheld a ruling in favour of the tour operator and a restaurant, finding that a liability waiver signed before the ride protected the operator against the negligence allegations.A pub crawl takes an unfortunate turnAccording to the Indiana Court of Appeals, Anthony Boarman joined a group of friends for a Handlebar pedal-bar tour through downtown Indianapolis on August 1, 2021. The mobile platform accommodates groups of up to 12 passengers, who sit facing inward around the vehicle. Its seats are approximately 48 inches above the ground, with pedals serving as steps to help passengers climb aboard.The two-hour experience included stops at Monument Circle, Condado Tacos and Coaches Tavern. Boarman brought a six-pack of beer for the outing and also consumed alcoholic drinks during the tour.At the end of the journey, as the group returned to its starting point, Boarman attempted to get down from the elevated seat as though he were stepping off an ordinary bar stool. He fell directly onto the pavement and sustained injuries.The waiver that became central to the caseBefore boarding, Boarman and his companions had electronically signed liability waivers. The documents released The Handlebar, its owners, and employees from claims for injuries or damages before, during, or after the tour, including company-caused incidents.In June 2023, Boarman sued The Handlebar, Coaches Tavern operator Isentark Entertainment, and others. His allegations included negligence and violations of Indiana's Dram Shop Act, which governs circumstances under which establishments can be held responsible for serving alcohol to intoxicated customers.The Indiana Court of Appeals noted that Boarman acknowledged signing the waiver and had not requested clarification about its provisions.Why negligence was rejectedA key argument for Boarman was that The Handlebar had not included the waiver as an affirmative defense in its initial response to his complaint. The appeals court ruled that the company could use it later despite the omission.At his September 2024 deposition, Boarman was allowed to rebut the defense about the document. He also failed to demonstrate that introducing the waiver later had prejudiced his case.Most importantly, the Indiana Court of Appeals ruled that the document's wording covered operator negligence injuries even though negligence was not explicitly mentioned.Consequently, the waiver barred Boarman's negligence claim against The Handlebar.Why the restaurant was also clearedThe court separately examined whether Coaches Tavern's operator could be held responsible under Indiana's Dram Shop Act.Under the relevant law, an establishment furnishing alcohol can face civil liability when it actually knows a customer is visibly intoxicated at the time of service and that intoxication subsequently causes an injury.The evidence did not establish that Boarman displayed obvious signs of intoxication while at the tavern. He had not stumbled, behaved belligerently or slurred his speech, and he did not experience difficulties getting back onto the pedal bar.The Indiana Court of Appeals therefore concluded that there was insufficient evidence that the restaurant's employees knew he was visibly intoxicated when serving him.Appeals court upholds the rulingThe Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's summary judgment in favour of both defendants and rejected Boarman's request to correct the earlier ruling.The November 6, 2026 memorandum decision emphasizes the need for properly drafted liability waivers and proof of liability under Indiana's alcohol-serving statutes. As a memorandum decision, it is not binding precedent under Indiana Appellate Rule 65(D), and the court noted that it cannot be relied upon until certified.Boarman won a five-year lawsuit when the original judgment was upheld. The case hinged on the signed waiver and the lack of evidence the tavern knew he was drunk.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron voiced support for Ukraine in its ongoing war against Russia, noting that “there is no more U.S. support.”

“Without Europeans … there is no support for Ukraine,” Macron told the press while attending the European Political Community Summit in Ireland, according to a clip posted Thursday on social platform X .

“We are those to support Ukraine, we are those to help them in the resistance war. There is no more U.S. support,” he added. “There is some mediations, fine, but at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”

Macron’s remarks come a day after Russia and Ukraine agreed to a “large-scale” exchange of prisoners of war after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has previously praised European leaders for their support of Ukraine, saying, “I am so thankful that we have such huge support from EU Council, Commission and leaders, real leaders so that they stay with us from the very beginning of this war.”

In recent weeks, the U.S. has acted as a mediator between Russia and Ukraine, although its own relations with Ukraine have grown tense over the Starlink slowdown in Ukraine and America’s diesel deal with Russia .

Zelensky has criticized President Trump for striking a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin on supplying diesel to the U.S. and the global market. Trump struck back during an interview on Newsmax, saying Zelensky is “not a good guy for us to deal with.”

Last month, first lady Melania Trump secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the front-line city of Oleshky. The temporary pause in conflict , which started at 3 a.m. local time on Oct. 27, was set to last through Oct. 31 to allow for the delivery of humanitarian aid. It was originally set to begin on Oct. 29.

Shortly before the Oleshky ceasefire announcement, Ukraine faced a Starlink slowdown , which restricted its access to Starshield.

Starlink services were cut off for objects that traveled more than 100 mph, impacting the capabilities of Ukraine’s drones, airplanes and helicopters. This sparked a backlash as well as finger-pointing as to who was behind the decision.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk initially claimed the choice to restrict the speed or usage of Starshield is made by the U.S. military, but later he alluded to being involved in the decision in a post on social media, writing, “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week.”

On Thursday, Zelensky said in a post on X that the country is again facing restrictions on Starshield.

“This means more Russian strikes get through, and more of our people are killed by Russia,” Zelensky said. “We are trying to get the details from the American side, but so far, we know very little.”

articles.title: Oklahoma dismisses murder charge against former death row inmate Richard Glossip
articles.summary: A murder charge against Richard Glossip, a former death row prisoner who was nearly executed multiple times, was dismissed on Thursday after being granted a retrial in the 1997 killing of his former boss, according to his attorney.
articles.body: A murder charge against Richard Glossip, a former death row prisoner who was nearly executed multiple times, was dismissed on Thursday after being granted a retrial in the 1997 killing of his former boss, according to his attorney. He was sentenced to death over the killing of a motel owner named Barry Van Treese, who was beaten to death with a baseball bat. Prosecutors alleged that Treese was killed in a murder-for-hire plot but Glossip has maintained his innocence for almost 30 years. His conviction was thrown out by the Supreme Court last year after finding issues with key witness testimony. The court determined that prosecutors admitted testimony they knew to be false, violating Glossip’s right to a fair trial. He served nearly 30 years in prison before being released on bond in May. Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond announced last year that he intended to retry Glossip on a first-degree murder charge, but without seeking the death penalty. But Drummond also agreed with the Supreme Court decision, saying it was “an undeniable fact that he did not receive a fair trial.” Glossip pleaded guilty to a lesser charge of being an accessory to murder after the fact Thursday morning in order to “put this matter to rest,” according to his attorney Don Knight. His sentencing will be held in December, his attorney said. Knight noted that Glossip would have been released a decade ago if prosecutors had originally convicted him of the accessory charge. “We look forward to an opportunity to show why returning him to custody would not serve the interests of justice, and to ending this nightmare for Rich and all concerned,” Knight said. Prosecutors intend to seek a maximum 45-year sentence, according to Drummond’s office. Drummond said that it was difficult decision, but that “this path ensures a conviction related to Mr. Van Treese’s murder and gives us the best chance to secure additional prison time for Glossip.” Since his 1998 conviction, Glossip has had nine execution dates scheduled. At least three times he has been served what was expected to be his last meal.

articles.title: Donald Trump Jr. defends Russell Brand after rape conviction, questions 10-year sentence; says ‘when he was married to Katy Perry, no one seemed to think he was a rapist then’
articles.summary: Donald Trump Jr.
articles.body: Donald Trump Jr. has joined several prominent conservative voices in defending British comedian Russell Brand after he was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault. In a video shared on X on November 10, US President Donald Trump's eldest son questioned the conviction and the length of the sentence, claiming Brand was prosecuted after embracing Christianity and expressing support for conservative ideas. He also questioned the absence of forensic evidence and suggested that the comedian was being treated unfairly by the British justice system.In the video, the 48-year-old businessman criticised the prosecution, claiming that Brand was convicted without forensic evidence, DNA or a police report from the time of the alleged offences."He was convicted, by the way, with no forensic evidence, no DNA, no police report from the time," Don Jr. said.He also questioned why allegations against Brand, some of which date back several years, had not resulted in criminal proceedings earlier. Referring to the comedian's past marriage to singer Katy Perry, he suggested that Brand's celebrity status had not attracted similar scrutiny at the time."So, when he was, like, married to Katy Perry and was one of the most famous actors in the world, no one seemed to have a problem. No one seemed to think he was a rapist then," he said.Trump Jr. then linked Brand's recent religious and political views to the timing of the prosecution, suggesting that his embrace of Christianity and conservative ideas had made him a target."He finds God, I guess, changes his ways, sees some aspects of conservative life and talks about them, and now he's going to spend 10-and-a-half years imprisoned for rape, when no one had a problem with it in the prior 27 years," he added.What happened in Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault case?Brand, 51, was sentenced at London's Southwark Crown Court on November 9, 2026, after a jury found him guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. The offences took place between 2004 and 2009. He was acquitted of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.During sentencing, Judge Joel Bennathan described Brand as a "sexual predator" and criticised his "staggering arrogance". The judge also said Brand's growing fame had enabled him to behave as though he was above the rules followed by others.Brand denied the charges and maintained that the sexual encounters were consensual. However, the jury found him guilty on four counts following a four-week trial.It is worth noting that while Trump Jr. referred to allegations dating back 27 years, the four offences resulting in Brand's convictions were committed between 2004 and 2009. The prosecution's case included testimony from the women, and the absence of DNA evidence does not mean there was no evidence before the court.Megyn Kelly and Elon Musk also defend Russell BrandTrump Jr. is not the only prominent conservative figure to question Brand's conviction and prison sentence.On the November 9 episode of The Megyn Kelly Show, broadcaster Megyn Kelly described the case as a "political witch hunt" and called the 10-and-a-half-year sentence "insane".Meanwhile, billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk also reacted to the development on X. Responding to another user's post about the sentence, Musk called it "unjust".The reactions have sparked further debate around Brand's conviction, the British justice system and the role of celebrity and political affiliations in public discussions surrounding criminal cases.Russell Brand's wife supported him during the trialBrand's wife, Laura Brand, was present during the court proceedings and had also given evidence in his defence. During the trial, she described her husband as "amazingly attentive" and "kind", telling the jury, "I love him very much."Despite Brand's continued denial of the allegations, the jury convicted him on four counts. The judge's sentence means he will serve two-thirds of his 10-year-and-six-month term before being released on licence, subject to the applicable conditions.You use AI every day. articles.title: Victims’ families lash out at Gavin Newsom after mass commutation of ‘monsters’ on death row in California
articles.summary: Loved ones of California murder victims lashed out at Gov. Gavin Newsom on Thursday, one week after he moved to commute the death sentences of more than 500 condemned inmates.
articles.body: Loved ones of California murder victims lashed out at Gov. Gavin Newsom on Thursday, one week after he moved to commute the death sentences of more than 500 condemned inmates. The executive action, considered to be one of the most consequential moves against capital punishment in recent history, angered crime victims who had already had to endure the agonizing pain of losing a relative. Faye Jenkins, whose daughter and son-in-law were tortured and murdered in their Riverside County home in 2008, said the California electorate backs capital punishment and Newsom shouldn’t have intervened. “We voted for this,” Jenkins told reporters outside the Orange County District Attorney’s Office in Santa Ana. “Who gives you that right to make the decision for all of us? You didn’t ask me, you didn’t ask my husband, you didn’t ask other families. Don’t inflict your personal beliefs on all of us.” Golden State voters were last asked about capital punishment in 2016 and then, by a relatively narrow margin, rejected a death penalty abolition measure. “People used to say they’re animals. No, I love animals. These were monsters,” Jenkins said of the four Marines who killed her daughter. “They tortured my daughter and made my (son-in-law) watch while they sexually assaulted her,” Jenkins said. “They stomped him and beat him so badly he even had shoe prints on his back — the impression where they stomped him so hard. Who does that? And these are people that (Newsom) thinks deserve a second chance?” Steve Herr, the father of Samuel Eliezer “Sam” Herr, recalled the 203 court dates he attended before neighbor Daniel Wozniak was convicted and sentenced to die for the killing of his son and the victim’s friend Juri “Julie” Kibuishi in Orange County in 2010. “He was sent to San Quentin’s death row to await his execution and I thought that was the end of that horrible nightmare,” Herr said. “That was not to be.” Representatives for Newsom did not immediately respond to an NBC News request for comment on Thursday. Newsom would need the consent of the California Supreme Court on 382 of the 548 condemned inmates to have them all moved off death row and to a sentence of life without the possibility of parole, or LWOP. However, Orange County DA Todd Spitzer insisted that there are procedural shortcuts around LWOP that could put these dangerous killers back on the street. “Life without the possibility of parole is absolute nonsense,” Spitzer said. “I have been so attacked through social media over the weekend and I’ve been responding to everybody that I see saying, ‘Todd, you’re fear mongering. You’re lying about the law. You know these people can’t get out of prison.’” “We practice law every day and we have people who’ve been sentenced to life without the possibility of parole who are getting out of prison,” he said. While there are mechanisms to gain parole following an LWOP sentence, Loyola Marymount University law professor Stan Goldman said he couldn’t think of an example of such an act off the top of his head. “As a practical matter, it’s not a real problem,” Goldman said Thursday. “If the past is prelude to future, it is very unlikely someone, or masses of people, will be released despite the fact they’ve been given LWOP after they were released from death row.”

articles.title: Scotland created Grand Theft Auto - is its video game industry still thriving?
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is set to become one of the biggest releases in history but how is the rest of Scotland's gaming industry doing?
articles.body:
As the world waits for the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, one of the most anticipated entertainment launches in history, its origins can still be traced back to a group of young developers working in Dundee almost 30 years ago.

The original GTA was built by Scottish studio DMA Design, laying the foundations for what would become one of the most successful video games franchises ever made.

"It was entirely the work of a Scottish team, all novices, we had no games design degrees at that point," says Brian Baglow, who worked as a writer on the game.

"The only people who believed in it were DMA Design. The publisher wanted to kill it," he says.

Over the last three decades, the game has sold hundreds of millions of copies while DMA Design became Rockstar North, moving to Edinburgh, and employing more than 1,000 people.

But while Rockstar is the superstar of Scotland's gaming industry, the story extends far beyond GTA.

Chris van der Kuyl, who co-founded VIS Entertainment in the early 1990s, says Scotland's games industry is almost unrecognisable from the one he entered 30-odd years ago.

"When we started out, people didn't think about Scotland at all," he says.

"There were a few people dotted around, but the main people were DMA in Dundee."

As the sector grew, more structured routes into games development began to emerge.

Abertay University in Dundee launched the world's first computer games degree in 1997, helping establish a formal pathway into the industry which Van der Kuyl says created a flow of new talent which was crucial to the industry's growth.

"Without a talent pipeline and new people coming into the industry, there would be no industry." van der Kuyl says.

In 2005, van der Kuyl co-founded Dundee-based 4J Studios, which went on to have huge success adapting Minecraft for consoles such as Xbox and Playstation.

He estimates that those console editions have sold about 70 million copies.

"There's no way you'd ever be able to predict that level of success for anything," he says.

His company now employs 57 people, a fraction of the size of Rockstar North but still one of the biggest games firms in Scotland.

Many of the other developers are small but still making a vital contribution to Scotland's reputation, van der Kuyl says.

"You've got companies that are only two or three people doing quite interesting stuff as indie developers." he says.

Scottish government figures show the number of games companies operating in Scotland was about 130 in 2024, up from just 15 in 2010.

Over the same period, industry turnover grew from £38.1m to £339.7m.

Van der Kuyl believes Scotland is now recognised internationally as one of the leading places to make games, comparing its reputation to established development hubs such as Sweden and the west coast of the United States.

Glasgow-based Screen Burn is another of Scotland's most successful independent game studios, employing 27 staff.

Formerly known as No Code, the studio earned a Bafta for Best British Game in 2020 with Observation, a sci-fi mystery that puts players in control of a space station's artificial intelligence.

The studio has recently attracted attention for its latest release, Silent Hill: Townfall, a new instalment in one of the world's most popular horror game franchises.

Rather than being handed an existing concept, the team pitched its own story, setting the game in a fictional Scottish town.

Screen Burn co-founder Jon McKellan says the project gave the studio a rare opportunity to put its own mark on an established franchise.

"This is our pitch, this was our story, we really put our stamp on it," he says.

For McKellan, Screen Burn's success demonstrates the growing diversity of Scotland's games industry, which now includes both global giants and independent studios.

But he says the dominance of Rockstar North can make it difficult for smaller companies to attract the same attention.

McKellan describes Rockstar as "a massive, immovable object" within Scotland's games sector.

"It's kind of like if you spend all your water on the one plant, you'll have one great tree and the rest of it will die out," he says.

His own career reflects some of those challenges.

After the Dundee studio where he landed his first job collapsed, McKellan says he had little choice but to leave Scotland to continue working in games.

"There were no other opportunities in Scotland at the time, it was either Rockstar or move down south," he says.

He spent five years in England before returning to Scotland to create his own studio.

While Scotland's games industry has expanded significantly, McKellan says sustaining a studio remains a challenge.

Unlike film and television, where work is often organised around individual productions, games companies often need to maintain teams through development cycles that can last several years, he says.

"We have people on salary that work year in, year out, whereas film tends to be short bursts of work," McKellan says.

McKellan says the biggest challenge is creating enough opportunities to sustain and grow studios in Scotland, with many graduates struggling to find work in the sector.

He says Scotland already has the creative talent to compete internationally, but needs more opportunities to keep developers in the country.

"We're maybe hiring one or two people a year, we can't absorb every graduate that's coming out." he says.

For McKellan, Screen Burn's work on Silent Hill: Townfall shows what smaller Scottish studios can achieve when given that chance.

"There's some really great talent in Scotland. If they're given the right opportunities, they can create a bit of a wave of cool content that people aren't expecting," he says.

For Baglow, who worked on the original GTA and is now a leading voice in Scotland's games industry, the continued success of the franchise shows the strength of the sector.

"The fact that not only has it achieved the success it has, but it's still being made here in Scotland, should be seen and championed as our biggest cultural export ever," he says.

Baglow says the biggest challenge facing developers today is not making games, but finding players.

With development tools becoming more widely available, more people and studios can create games than ever before, he says.

While this has made development easier, it has also made competition for audiences increasingly intense.

"The challenges facing developers is not making video games, it's now user acquisition, as in finding players," he says.

Baglow says studios can find themselves needing a major commercial hit to survive.

"That need for a breakout consumer hit, and if you don't get it, it kills your studio," he says.

However, Baglow says that the expertise built within game studios - including user engagement, digital design and 3D visualisation - could be applied in other industries, ranging from healthcare and education to financial services.

"Any sector that is struggling either to build engagement with a user, a consumer, a player, or needs to teach its staff and train its staff up, there's a role for video games in all of that," he says.

For Baglow, Scotland's challenge is no longer proving it can create successful games, it is ensuring the industry has the investment and support needed to build on that success.

articles.title: Jensen Huang's 2nd affair fallout shakes up US
articles.summary: The TOI correspondent from Washington: A second alleged extra-marital affair brought down Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Thursday after the company board
articles.body: The TOI correspondent from Washington: A second alleged extra-marital affair brought down Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Thursday after the company board initially appeared to stand by him following glowing testimonials from President Donald Trump, who repeatedly vouched for his character despite reports of his being entrapped by a Chinese spy.The Nvidia board's Nov 8 statement had struck a reassuring note, expressing confidence in Huang and asserting there was no reason to believe that Nvidia's national security or corporate secrets had been compromised, while announcing an independent investigation into the matter. Four days later the confidence evaporated after the second alleged affair, which company insiders were apparently aware of, was leaked to the NYT.Beyond the turmoil at Nvidia, where Huang's two adult children, Madison and Spencer, have director-level roles, there is now considerable embarrassment for President Trump, who invested political capital vouching for Huang's character. He called him an "honourable man" and a "great guy who... has done an amazing job for our country." Hours after Huang quit, Trump did not address the scandal but said in a post on Truth Social, "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!"But the fallout from the scandal goes beyond the Nvidia boardroom and the tech world. It is already shaking up Washington's political establishment, drawing in Trump's cabinet secretaries, some of whom were at odds with each other, as intelligence reports emerged over the past year about Huang's affair with the alleged Chinese spy. Democrats are also champing at the bit to begin investigations and hearings into the matter.According to several accounts, it was secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is also the US national security adviser, who supervised a classified intelligence memorandum warning the administration about Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Rubio is also reported to have personally briefed Trump aboard Air Force One in May, before Huang joined the presidential delegation in Alaska for the onward flight to China.The controversy has also drawn in commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and treasury secretary Scott Bessent. According to a report in Axios, Bessent raised the question of the administration's failure to place Megaspeed, allegedly a front company Alice Huang worked for, on the commerce department's Entity List, which would restrict its access to American technology. Lutnick, who, like Huang, has argued that excessive restrictions risk sacrificing commercial opportunities and provoking a trade war, reportedly muttered that he needed to check with Trump.Trump himself has been careful about ratcheting up temperature on the affair given an upcoming meeting next week with China's President Xi Jinping at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, and Nvidia's criticality to not just American tech primacy but also to the US stock market, a Trump obsession which he seems to believe is an indicator of economic health.You use AI every day.
